slides.title: The night sky is a time machine

source.value:
A six-minute field guide to now

# The night sky is a time machine

Look up. Nothing you see is happening now.

Observation begins with delay

Open by letting the room sit with the contradiction. “The sky feels immediate, but every point in it is a delayed message.” Use the dial from the inside out: Moon, Sun, then Andromeda. The conceptual move is simple: distance and time are the same measurement when the messenger has a speed limit.

speakerNotes.plainText: At first, point only to the source and observer. Reveal the first line: a finite speed turns separation into delay. Reveal the second: a photon carries information about the state of its source when it left. Avoid saying that we see “where the object used to be” in every case; the precise claim here is that we see an earlier state.

01 · The courier

## Light arrives late

A telescope does not pull the present closer. It catches an older message.

Distance sets the delivery time.
The image is the message that survived the trip.

speakerNotes.plainText: Read the ladder quickly, without turning it into trivia. Moonlight is a little over a second old. Sunlight left before this sentence began. Sirius is a childhood photograph on a cosmic scale. Andromeda’s light began crossing space before our species existed. The values are rounded for spoken clarity.

02 · The distance ladder

## Every distance is a date

Farther does not only mean smaller. It means earlier.

One rule · four scales

Read the ladder quickly, without turning it into trivia. Moonlight is a little over a second old. Sunlight left before this sentence began. Sirius is a childhood photograph on a cosmic scale. Andromeda’s light began crossing space before our species existed. The values are rounded for spoken clarity.

speakerNotes.plainText: The dark lines are the fingerprint. The same pattern appears in both bars, but every observed line has moved toward the red end. That displacement is evidence, not an artist’s metaphor: astronomers compare known spectral features with what arrives. Keep the explanation qualitative; the purpose is to show how old light carries both an image of its source and a record of its journey.

03 · The fingerprint

## Old light records the journey

Expansion stretches its wavelengths, but the pattern survives. That makes cosmic history measurable.

Same fingerprint · longer wavelength

speakerNotes.plainText: Stars had not yet formed when this light was released. Roughly 380,000 years after the Big Bang, electrons and nuclei combined into neutral atoms, and photons could travel freely. We observe that relic today as the cosmic microwave background. The timeline is conceptual rather than linear-to-scale; its job is to isolate the release event inside a 13.8-billion-year story.

slides.title: The oldest light is not starlight

source.value:
04 · The horizon

## The oldest light is not starlight

It escaped when the young universe cooled enough to become transparent.

Lookback horizon ≈ 13.8B years

We see that afterglow from every direction: a baby picture with no outside edge.
Stars had not yet formed when this light was released. Roughly 380,000 years after the Big Bang, electrons and nuclei combined into neutral atoms, and photons could travel freely. speakerNotes.plainText: Close with an action, not another fact. Suggest an easy first target: Vega’s light is about 25 years old, while the bright center of Andromeda is roughly 2.5 million years old. Ask the audience to name one of those ages aloud the next time they look up. Pause on the final line.

Choose one light. Find its distance. Then say the age of the message arriving at your eyes.

The sky is not a ceiling. It is an archive in transit.

manifest.title: Drever Basic
manifest.summary: A neutral visual baseline with generous space, clear typography, and focused motion.

principles: Give every slide one dominant idea
Use scale and space before decoration
Animate changes that clarify state or continuity
Prefer a meaningful visual over a longer list
avoid: More than two competing accent colors
Using a two-column layout when the ideas are unrelated

guidance: Use focus to keep prior evidence visible while making the current Step unmistakable.
Use replace for one changing state, compare for cumulative evidence, and stagger for at most four tightly related items.
Set flow to block for a vertical reading sequence and inline for a horizontal process or comparison; leave it unset when neither axis explains the content.
Basic motion uses clean fades and short spatial travel, keeping the content more prominent than the choreography.
Reuse a continuity name only when the same visual object persists across adjacent slides.

layouts.name: Cover
layouts.description: Open a presentation or major chapter with one concise title and restrained supporting context.

slots.purpose: An optional short category, event, or chapter label.

slots.name: title
slots.purpose: The single dominant statement for the slide.

slots.name: supporting
slots.purpose: One short sentence that adds context without repeating the title.

slots.name: footer
slots.purpose: Optional speaker, organization, date, or section metadata.

layouts.name: TwoColumn
layouts.description: Place two related ideas side by side when their relationship is more important than either idea alone.
